reuse.why: It uses the existing getApproxNumberThreshold and getRangeAmount and has getScheduledAmount delegate, though it adds a getExpectedAmount next to getScheduledAmount when the existing function already covered null, number and range.

duplication.why: Four inline null/number/range dispatches (updateActions, postTransactionForSchedule, preview, forecast) plus the template's op check collapse into one function, so the diff removes duplication.

placement.why: The rule sits in shared/schedules.ts next to getRangeAmount, and the tolerance comes from shared/rules.

scope.why: The diff only touches the amount callers, one test block and a release note.

maintainability.why: There is a single definition, but the op is an optional trailing parameter, so a caller that forgets it silently plans at the nominal value. The two overlapping entry points (getExpectedAmount and getScheduledAmount) need a comment on which to use.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Server paths all go through getExpectedAmount. The desktop-client callers keep calling getScheduledAmount without an op, which reaches the definition but not the approximate rule.

disguised_duplication.where: The earlier copies are removed and routed to the shared function.

one_place.where: The rule is defined once in getExpectedAmount (shared/schedules.ts) and used by every server path and the API, but desktop-client Balance.tsx and MobileSchedulesPage/SchedulesTable still call getScheduledAmount(schedule._amount) without the op, so the projected balance does not get the approximate rule.
